context:
Goal: a grant you type in one session reaches the session it names.
Problem (rule): auto mode in each session counts only words typed in its own chat, so a grant had to be typed again in each session, and the plan waits on your word before any build.
Based on (read): draft PR #1049: the receiving session reads your own typed message from the server, then checks the named act itself before auto mode sees it, since text added by a script never counts as your words.
Based on (read): the plan's recommended picks: a fixed grant wording, not free text; the first grants are merge and self-edit; a self-edit grant also covers the target's agents, a merge grant stays with the lead session; test the check that runs before each tool call first; the server-read path only; keep today's cloud merge rule.
Departs from: main — adds a grant relay path: a session acts on a grant you typed in another session.
holds: Building the grant relay, and the later step that lets an answer saved on this page count as your words.

lastAnswer.note: Lane grant-reaches-lanes (PR #1049) files it; closes when it lands.

options.gain: One grant reaches the session it names; no free-text grant can widen by a misread.
options.how: Every question takes the plan's recommended pick, listed above, and a lane builds the server-read path.
options.label: Sign off as written
options.lose: Only the listed grant wordings work; a new kind of grant needs a plan change.

options.gain: The plan matches what you want before anything is built.
options.how: Say in your reply which picks to change, for example: free-text grants judged by a model; merge grants only at first; grants for the lead session only, not its agents; or a cloud merge rule that needs a merge grant for every merge.
options.label: Sign off with changes

ref: draft PR #1049, docs/plans/grant-reaches-lanes.md, section 6; roadmap step grant-reaches-lanes
title: Sign off the plan for grants that reach another session, as written or with changes?
why: You said a grant typed in one session should count in the session it names. The plan in draft PR #1049 does that; nothing is built until you sign off its seven questions.
